Entity resolution systems typically employ machine learning and artificial intelligence models to tackle this challenge. The models use contextual information to predict whether or not two records refer to the same entity. For example, we can approximately resolve unique inventors by using patent topic, co-authors, employer, and location, in addition to first and last names

Instead of reviewing pairs of records, our evaluation approach utilizes a sample of fully-resolved entities, i.e., ground truth, or known clusters. In this approach, all pairs within a resolved cluster are known to match, and any pair that intersects a resolved cluster but is not contained within it is known to be a non-match.
